name: Oldowan industry
desc: The earliest stone tool tradition: simple choppers and sharp flakes struck from river cobbles.

name: Bone tools
desc: Implements shaped from bone and antler, later used for awls, needles, points and harpoons.

name: Hand axe
desc: The bifacially flaked Acheulean tool, used across Africa and Eurasia for over a million years.

name: Cooking
desc: Heating food to make it safer and more digestible, which reshaped human diet and anatomy.

name: Levallois technique
desc: A prepared-core method that let knappers plan and strike flakes of predetermined shape.

name: Hafting
desc: Attaching stone points or blades to wooden handles or shafts to make composite tools.

name: Birch tar
desc: An adhesive distilled from birch bark by heating, the oldest known synthetic material.

name: Beads
desc: Perforated shells and stones strung as ornaments, early evidence of symbolic culture.

name: Pressure flaking
desc: Removing fine flakes by pressing with a bone or antler tool, giving sharp, precise edges.

name: Raft
desc: Logs or reeds lashed into a floating platform, likely used in the settlement of Australia.

name: Tally stick
desc: Notched bones and sticks used to record counts, the earliest physical aids to arithmetic.

name: Burin
desc: A chisel-edged flint tool for engraving and working bone, antler and wood.

name: Lithic blades
desc: Long, parallel-sided flakes struck from prepared cores, typical of the Upper Paleolithic.

name: Tent
desc: A portable shelter of hides or fabric stretched over poles.

name: Footwear
desc: Protective coverings for the feet, from hide wraps to sewn shoes and sandals.

name: Ground stone tools
desc: Tools shaped by grinding and polishing rather than flaking, such as querns and polished axes.

name: Mortar and pestle
desc: A bowl and club for crushing seeds, pigments and medicines.

name: Microliths
desc: Tiny standardized stone blades set in rows into handles and arrows.

name: Stone boiling
desc: Heating water in skin, bark or basket containers by dropping in hot stones.

name: Earth oven
desc: A pit lined with heated stones for slow-cooking food, one of the oldest cooking structures.

name: Net
desc: A mesh of knotted cord used to catch fish, birds and small game.

name: Fish hook
desc: A bent or barbed point of shell, bone and later metal for catching fish.

name: Oil lamp
desc: A hollowed stone or clay vessel burning fat or oil through a wick for portable light.

name: Basket weaving
desc: Interlacing plant fibers into containers, mats and traps.

name: Ladder
desc: A frame of rungs for climbing, depicted in Mesolithic rock art.

name: Water well
desc: A shaft dug to reach groundwater, allowing settlement away from rivers.

name: Adze
desc: A hafted cutting tool with a transverse blade for shaping timber.

name: Bow drill
desc: A bowstring wrapped around a spindle to spin it fast, used to drill beads and to make fire.

name: Fire striker
desc: Striking flint against pyrite or later steel to throw sparks onto tinder.

name: Candle
desc: A wick embedded in solid tallow or wax, a cheap and portable source of light.

name: Mirror
desc: A reflecting surface, first of polished obsidian, later of bronze and silvered glass.

name: Comb
desc: A toothed tool of bone, wood or shell for grooming hair.

name: Cosmetics
desc: Ground minerals and pigments such as kohl and ochre applied to the body.

name: Board games
desc: Games with pieces on a marked surface, such as Senet and the Royal Game of Ur.

name: Dice
desc: Marked cubes of bone or stone used as random number generators in games.

name: Soap
desc: Fats boiled with alkaline ash, recorded in Babylon, used for washing and textiles.

name: Indus Valley sanitation
wiki: Sanitation of the Indus Valley Civilisation
desc: Covered brick drains, bathrooms and toilets serving whole cities like Mohenjo-daro.

name: Plumbing
desc: Pipes of clay, copper and lead that carry water into buildings and waste out of them.

name: Lock and key
desc: A mechanism that secures a door or box, from Egyptian wooden pin locks to metal locks.

name: Button
desc: A small disc or knob used first as an ornament, later as a fastener joining pieces of clothing.

name: Scissors
desc: Paired blades for cutting, first as spring shears and later pivoted.

name: Fibula brooch
desc: A spring-pin clothing fastener of the Bronze and Iron Ages, ancestor of the safety pin.

name: Chopsticks
desc: Paired sticks for cooking and eating, widespread in East Asia.

name: Perfume
desc: Aromatic oils extracted from plants and resins, recorded by the Mesopotamian chemist Tapputi.

name: Cloaca Maxima
desc: Rome's great covered sewer, among the earliest large municipal drainage systems.

name: Umbrella
desc: A canopy on a pole for shade or rain; collapsible versions appeared in ancient China.

name: Yakhchal
desc: A Persian domed ice house that stored ice through desert summers.

name: Hypocaust
desc: Roman underfloor heating that circulated hot furnace gases beneath raised floors.

name: Clothes iron
desc: A heated metal tool for pressing cloth, first a pan of hot coals in Han China.

name: Toilet paper
desc: Paper for personal hygiene, first recorded in 6th-century China.

name: Playing cards
desc: Printed card decks for games, spreading from Tang China to Europe.

name: Chimney
desc: A flue that draws smoke out of a building, enabling fireplaces in multi-room houses.

name: Toothbrush
desc: A handle with animal bristles for cleaning teeth, recorded in Ming China.

name: Flush toilet
desc: A toilet that washes waste away with water, designed by John Harington.

name: Pressure cooking
desc: Cooking in a sealed vessel above water's normal boiling point, pioneered by Denis Papin.

name: Kitchen stove
desc: An enclosed firebox with cooking holes, replacing open-hearth cooking.

name: Franklin stove
desc: Benjamin Franklin's metal-lined fireplace that radiated more heat into the room.

name: Shower
desc: A hand-pumped overhead spray for bathing, patented by William Feetham.

name: Plumbing trap
desc: Alexander Cumming's S-bend, a water seal that blocks sewer gas from entering homes.

name: Lever tumbler lock
desc: A lock with multiple levers that must all be lifted correctly, much harder to pick.

name: Argand lamp
desc: An oil lamp with a hollow wick and glass chimney that burned far brighter and cleaner.

name: Gas lighting
desc: Lighting with coal gas piped to burners, which lit factories and city streets.

name: Bleach
desc: Chlorine compounds for whitening cloth and disinfecting, made cheaply as bleaching powder.

name: Icebox
desc: An insulated cabinet cooled by blocks of ice, the domestic forerunner of the refrigerator.

name: Slow sand filter
desc: Water purification by percolation through sand beds, first used for a town supply in Paisley.

name: Fire extinguisher
desc: A portable pressurized container of water or chemicals for putting out fires.

name: Döbereiner's lamp
desc: A hydrogen lighter ignited by a platinum catalyst, the first commercial lighter.

name: Friction match
desc: A stick tipped with chemicals that ignites when struck, invented by John Walker.

name: Gas stove
desc: A cooking stove fueled by piped gas, giving instant, controllable heat.

name: Lawn mower
desc: Edwin Budding's reel mower, which made close-cut lawns practical.

name: Central heating
desc: Heating a whole building from one boiler through pipes of hot water or steam.

name: Silvered glass mirror
desc: Justus von Liebig's chemical deposition of silver on glass, making cheap clear mirrors.

name: Sanitary sewer
desc: Underground pipe networks that carry household sewage away from cities.

name: Safety match
desc: A match that ignites only on a special striking surface, using red phosphorus.

name: Pin tumbler lock
desc: The Yale cylinder lock with spring pins, still the most common door lock.

name: Safety pin
desc: Walter Hunt's bent wire pin with a clasp that shields the point.

name: Washing machine
desc: A machine that agitates clothes in water; electric models were advertised from 1904.

name: Kerosene lamp
desc: A wick lamp burning refined kerosene, the main domestic light before electricity.

name: Burglar alarm
desc: An electric circuit that rings a bell when a door or window is opened.

name: Can opener
desc: A hand tool for cutting open sealed tin cans.

name: Septic tank
desc: An underground tank where sewage settles and decomposes, for homes off the sewer network.

name: London sewerage system
desc: Joseph Bazalgette's intercepting sewers, which ended London's cholera epidemics.

name: Water heater
desc: A gas-fired appliance that supplies hot water on demand to a home.

name: Carpet sweeper
desc: A push device with rotating brushes that lifts dirt from carpets.

name: Cash register
desc: James Ritty's mechanical till that recorded sales and deterred theft.

name: Safety razor
desc: A razor with a guard over the blade; disposable blades followed in 1901.

name: Electric fan
desc: A motor-driven fan that cools rooms by moving air.

name: Vending machine
desc: A coin-operated machine that dispenses goods without a clerk.

name: Thermostat
desc: A device that switches heating on and off to hold a set temperature.

name: Gas mantle
desc: Welsbach's mesh of rare-earth oxides that glows white-hot, greatly brightening gas lamps.

name: Snap fastener
desc: A pair of interlocking metal discs that press together to fasten clothing.

name: Dishwasher
desc: Josephine Cochrane's machine that sprayed hot water onto racked dishes.

name: Electric kettle
desc: A kettle with an internal electric heating element for boiling water.

name: Vacuum flask
desc: James Dewar's double-walled evacuated vessel that keeps liquids hot or cold.

name: Electric stove
desc: A cooking range heated by electric resistance elements.

name: Toaster
desc: An electric appliance that browns bread with glowing heating wires.

name: Flashlight
desc: A portable battery-powered electric light.

name: Paper clip
desc: A bent steel wire that holds sheets of paper together.

name: Vacuum cleaner
desc: A machine that sucks dust from floors; Hubert Booth's version began powered cleaning.

name: Air conditioning
desc: Willis Carrier's system for cooling and dehumidifying indoor air.

name: Plugs and sockets
desc: Detachable connectors that let appliances draw mains electricity from wall outlets.

name: Water chlorination
desc: Disinfecting public water supplies with chlorine, which sharply cut typhoid deaths.

name: Aluminium foil
desc: Thin rolled aluminium sheet for wrapping and preserving food.

name: Refrigerator
desc: The electric household refrigerator, which transformed food storage and diet.

name: Zipper
desc: Gideon Sundback's interlocking-tooth slide fastener for clothing and bags.

name: Activated sludge
desc: Treating sewage by aerating it with microbes, the basis of modern wastewater plants.

name: Clothes dryer
desc: A heated tumbling drum that dries laundry indoors.

name: Synthetic detergent
desc: Synthetic surfactants that clean in hard water where soap forms scum.

name: Blender
desc: A motorized jar with spinning blades for mixing and pureeing food.

name: Garbage disposal unit
desc: A sink-mounted grinder that shreds food waste into the sewer.

name: Electric razor
desc: Jacob Schick's motor-driven dry shaver.

name: Microwave oven
desc: An oven that heats food with microwaves from a magnetron, found by radar engineer Percy Spencer.

name: Electric rice cooker
desc: An automatic cooker that switches off when rice is done, transforming Asian kitchens.

name: Hook-and-loop fastener
desc: George de Mestral's Velcro, two nylon strips of hooks and loops that grip each other.

name: Residual-current device
desc: A safety switch that cuts power when current leaks to earth, preventing electrocution.

name: Smoke detector
desc: A battery-powered ionization alarm that warns of fire in the home.

name: Induction cooking
desc: Heating pans directly by electromagnetic induction from a coil under the hob.

name: Keycard lock
desc: A lock opened by a coded card, now standard in hotels and offices.

name: Robotic vacuum cleaner
desc: An autonomous floor-cleaning robot that navigates a home with sensors.

name: Smart thermostat
desc: A networked, learning thermostat that schedules heating and can be controlled remotely.

name: Smart speaker
desc: A voice-controlled speaker with a built-in assistant that also runs home automation.

name: Banking
desc: Lending and deposit-taking, from Mesopotamian temples to Italian banking houses.

name: Banknote
desc: Paper money issued by a bank and payable to the bearer on demand; the Song Chinese Jiaozi is the earliest example.

name: Double-entry bookkeeping
desc: Recording every transaction as matching debit and credit, the basis of modern accounting.

name: Marine insurance
desc: Contracts that spread the risk of losing ships and cargo, the first modern insurance.

name: Patent
desc: A temporary legal monopoly granted to inventors, starting with the Venetian statute of 1474.

name: Joint-stock company
desc: A firm owned by tradable shares, pioneered by the Dutch East India Company.

name: Stock exchange
desc: A market for trading company shares, beginning in Amsterdam.

name: Central bank
desc: A state institution managing currency and credit, starting with Sweden's Riksbank.

name: Wire transfer
desc: Sending money by telegraph message between bank offices.

name: Credit card
desc: A payment card that lets holders buy on credit; Diners Club's 1950 general-purpose charge card was an early forerunner.

name: Barcode
desc: Machine-readable patterns of bars encoding data, patented by Woodland and Silver.

name: Magnetic stripe card
desc: A plastic card with a magnetic data strip, developed at IBM.

name: Automated teller machine
desc: A machine that dispenses cash without a teller, first installed by Barclays in London.

name: Universal Product Code
desc: The retail barcode standard, first scanned at a supermarket checkout in 1974.

name: Smart card
desc: A plastic card with an embedded chip, used for payment, phones and identity.

name: QR code
desc: A two-dimensional matrix barcode developed by Denso Wave, later used for mobile payments.

name: Contactless payment
desc: Paying by tapping a card or device against a reader using short-range radio.

name: M-Pesa
desc: A phone-based money transfer service in Kenya that brought banking to millions.

name: Units of measurement
desc: Standardized lengths, weights and volumes such as the cubit, needed for trade and building.

name: Sexagesimal system
desc: Babylonian base-60 counting, still used for time and angles.

name: Pythagorean theorem
desc: The relation between the sides of a right triangle, known in Babylon and later proven by the Greeks.

name: Method of exhaustion
desc: Finding areas and volumes by inscribing ever finer polygons, a forerunner of integration.

name: Syllogistic logic
desc: Aristotle's formal system of deductive argument, the start of logic as a discipline.

name: Euclidean algorithm
desc: A step-by-step procedure for the greatest common divisor, among the oldest algorithms.

name: Archimedes' principle
desc: The buoyant force on a body equals the weight of fluid it displaces.

name: Measuring Earth's circumference
desc: Eratosthenes' estimate of Earth's size from shadow angles at two cities.

name: Negative numbers
desc: Numbers below zero, used for debts in Han China and later in India.

name: Trigonometry
desc: Hipparchus' tables of chords relating angles and lengths, essential to astronomy and surveying.

name: Almagest
desc: Ptolemy's mathematical model of planetary motion, the standard astronomy text for 1,400 years.

name: Ptolemy's Geography
desc: A world atlas using latitude and longitude coordinates and map projections.

name: Sine function
desc: Aryabhata's half-chord tables, the trigonometric functions used ever since.

name: Zero
desc: Brahmagupta's treatment of zero as a number with rules of arithmetic.

name: Book of Optics
desc: Ibn al-Haytham's experimental study of light and vision.

name: Complex numbers
desc: Numbers with an imaginary part, introduced by Cardano and later vital to physics and engineering.

name: Logarithm
desc: John Napier's method of turning multiplication into addition, which sped up calculation.

name: Analytic geometry
desc: Descartes' coordinates that describe curves with equations.

name: Probability theory
desc: The mathematics of chance, founded in Pascal and Fermat's letters on gambling.

name: Statistics
desc: Collecting and analyzing numerical data, begun with John Graunt's mortality tables.

name: Differential equations
desc: Equations relating quantities to their rates of change, used to model physical systems.

name: Binary numbers
desc: Leibniz's base-2 arithmetic, later the native language of digital computers.

name: Normal distribution
desc: The bell curve, found by de Moivre, central to statistics and error analysis.

name: Graph theory
desc: Euler's study of networks of nodes and edges, begun with the Königsberg bridges.

name: Bayes' theorem
desc: A rule for updating probabilities with new evidence.

name: Modular arithmetic
desc: Gauss's arithmetic of remainders, later the core of public-key cryptography.

name: Least squares
desc: Fitting a model to data by minimizing squared errors, from Legendre and Gauss.

name: Fourier analysis
desc: Decomposing functions into sums of sine waves, essential to signals, sound and imaging.

name: Non-Euclidean geometry
desc: Consistent geometries where Euclid's parallel postulate fails, later used by general relativity.

name: Group theory
desc: The algebra of symmetry, begun by Galois, now basic to physics and cryptography.

name: Matrix algebra
desc: Rectangular arrays of numbers and their algebra, formalized by Cayley.

name: Control theory
desc: The mathematics of feedback, started by Maxwell's analysis of governors.

name: Set theory
desc: Cantor's theory of collections and infinities, a foundation for all of mathematics.

name: First-order logic
desc: Frege's formal logic with quantifiers, the basis of mathematical logic.

name: Vector calculus
desc: Gibbs and Heaviside's notation for fields in three dimensions.

name: Regression analysis
desc: Galton's method for estimating relationships between variables.

name: Statistical hypothesis testing
desc: Fisher's framework for judging whether data support a claim, standard in experimental science.

name: Game theory
desc: Von Neumann's mathematics of strategic decision-making.

name: Gödel's incompleteness theorems
desc: Proof that any consistent formal system of arithmetic has unprovable truths.

name: Kolmogorov axioms
desc: The rigorous axiomatic foundation of probability theory.

name: Theory of computation
desc: Turing and Church's formal definition of what can be computed by an algorithm.

name: Monte Carlo method
desc: Solving problems by random sampling on a computer, devised for nuclear weapons work.

name: Linear programming
desc: Optimizing a linear objective under constraints; Dantzig's simplex method made it practical.

name: Information theory
desc: Shannon's measure of information and channel capacity, the basis of digital communication.

name: Cybernetics
desc: Wiener's study of control and communication in machines and living things.

name: Sampling theorem
desc: How often a signal must be sampled to be reconstructed, the basis of digital audio and video.

name: Error-correcting codes
desc: Hamming's codes that detect and fix transmission errors, used in memory, disks and links.

name: Finite element method
desc: Solving engineering equations by dividing structures into small elements on a computer.

name: Kalman filter
desc: An algorithm that estimates a system's state from noisy measurements, used in navigation.

name: Chaos theory
desc: Lorenz's finding that deterministic systems can be unpredictable, limiting weather forecasts.

name: Fast Fourier transform
desc: The Cooley-Tukey algorithm that made spectral analysis fast enough for everyday computing.

name: Computational complexity theory
desc: Classifying problems by the time and memory needed to solve them.

name: Fractal geometry
desc: Mandelbrot's geometry of self-similar shapes, used in modeling and graphics.

name: Heliocentrism
desc: Copernicus' Sun-centered model of the solar system.

name: Kepler's laws
desc: Elliptical orbits and the laws governing planetary speeds.

name: Pascal's law
desc: Pressure in a confined fluid is transmitted equally, the principle of hydraulic machines.

name: Boyle's law
desc: The inverse relation between a gas's pressure and volume.

name: Stratigraphy
desc: Steno's principle that rock layers record time in sequence, the basis of geology.

name: Hooke's law
desc: Extension of a spring is proportional to force, the basis of elasticity and spring scales.

name: Speed of light measurement
wiki: Rømer's determination of the speed of light
desc: Rømer's demonstration from Jupiter's moons that light travels at a finite speed.

name: Universal gravitation
desc: Newton's inverse-square law of gravity uniting celestial and terrestrial motion.

name: Bernoulli's principle
desc: Faster fluid flow means lower pressure, key to aerodynamics and hydraulics.

name: Coulomb's law
desc: The inverse-square law of force between electric charges.

name: Atomic theory
desc: Dalton's theory that elements consist of atoms combining in fixed ratios.

name: Ohm's law
desc: Current is proportional to voltage divided by resistance, the basis of circuit design.

name: Faraday's law of induction
desc: A changing magnetic field induces a voltage, the principle of generators and transformers.

name: Ideal gas law
desc: Clapeyron's equation linking a gas's pressure, volume and temperature.

name: Doppler effect
desc: The change in observed frequency of a wave from a moving source, used in radar and astronomy.

name: Navier-Stokes equations
desc: Equations describing viscous fluid flow, central to engineering and weather models.

name: Conservation of energy
desc: Energy is neither created nor destroyed, only converted between forms.

name: Greenhouse effect
desc: Eunice Foote and John Tyndall showed that carbon dioxide and water vapor trap heat.

name: Kinetic theory of gases
desc: Explains gas pressure and temperature as the motion of molecules.

name: Entropy
desc: Clausius' measure of disorder, which sets the limits of every heat engine.

name: Periodic table
desc: Mendeleev's arrangement of elements by recurring properties, which predicted new elements.

name: Statistical mechanics
desc: Boltzmann and Gibbs' derivation of thermodynamics from the statistics of particles.

name: Electromagnetic waves
desc: Hertz's demonstration of the waves Maxwell predicted, the basis of radio.

name: Photoelectric effect
desc: Light ejecting electrons from metal, explained by Einstein in 1905 with light quanta.

name: Radioactivity
desc: Becquerel's discovery that some elements emit radiation spontaneously.

name: Electron
desc: J. J. Thomson's discovery of the first subatomic particle, the carrier of electric current.

name: Planck's law
desc: Black-body radiation explained by quantized energy, the start of quantum theory.

name: Special relativity
desc: Einstein's theory that the speed of light is constant and time and space are relative.

name: Mass-energy equivalence
desc: E = mc², showing mass and energy are interchangeable, the basis of nuclear power.

name: Radiometric dating
desc: Dating rocks by radioactive decay, which established Earth's great age.

name: Atomic nucleus
desc: Rutherford's discovery that an atom's mass sits in a tiny positive core.

name: Superconductivity
desc: Zero electrical resistance in some materials at very low temperatures, found by Kamerlingh Onnes.

name: Bohr model
desc: Electrons in quantized orbits, explaining atomic spectra.

name: Isotopes
desc: Soddy's finding that an element can have atoms of different mass.

name: General relativity
desc: Einstein's theory of gravity as curved spacetime, needed today for GPS accuracy.

name: Chemical bond theory
desc: Lewis' electron-pair account of how atoms bond, later grounded in quantum mechanics.

name: Electronic band theory
desc: Bloch's theory of electron energy bands in solids, which explains semiconductors.

name: Neutron
desc: Chadwick's uncharged nuclear particle, the key to nuclear fission.

name: Quantum electrodynamics
desc: The quantum field theory of light and matter, the most precisely tested theory in physics.

name: Standard Model
desc: The theory of all known elementary particles and three of the four forces.

name: Higgs boson discovery
desc: Confirmation at CERN's Large Hadron Collider of the particle that gives others mass.

name: Gravitational wave detection
desc: LIGO's laser interferometers detected ripples in spacetime from merging black holes.

name: Linnaean taxonomy
desc: Linnaeus' hierarchical classification and two-part names for living things.

name: Cell theory
desc: Schleiden and Schwann's principle that all organisms are made of cells.

name: Evolution by natural selection
desc: Darwin and Wallace's mechanism for how species change and diversify.

name: Weather forecasting
desc: FitzRoy's storm warnings built from telegraphed observations.

name: Mendelian inheritance
desc: Mendel's laws of heredity from pea experiments, rediscovered in 1900.

name: Chromosome theory of inheritance
desc: The finding that genes are carried on chromosomes.

name: Continental drift
desc: Wegener's proposal that continents move across Earth's surface.

name: Modern evolutionary synthesis
desc: The merger of Darwinian evolution with Mendelian and population genetics.

name: Radiocarbon dating
desc: Libby's method of dating organic remains by carbon-14 decay, transforming archaeology.

name: Numerical weather prediction
desc: Forecasting weather by solving atmospheric equations on computers, first done on ENIAC.

name: Central dogma of molecular biology
desc: Crick's principle that sequence information, once in protein, cannot flow back to protein or nucleic acid.

name: Genetic code
desc: The triplet code by which DNA sequences specify amino acids, deciphered 1961 to 1966.

name: Seafloor spreading
desc: Hess's finding that new ocean crust forms at mid-ocean ridges.

name: Plate tectonics
desc: The theory that Earth's crust moves as rigid plates, explaining earthquakes and mountains.

name: Climate model
desc: Manabe and Wetherald's computer model predicting warming from rising carbon dioxide.

name: Cartography
desc: Making maps, from the Babylonian world map to modern atlases.

name: Julian calendar
desc: Julius Caesar's 365-day solar calendar with a leap day every four years.

name: Triangulation surveying
desc: Mapping land by measuring angles in networks of triangles, described by Gemma Frisius.

name: Mercator projection
desc: A map projection that shows lines of constant compass bearing as straight lines.

name: Gregorian calendar
desc: The reformed calendar that corrected drift against the seasons, now used worldwide.

name: Metric system
desc: Decimal units based on natural standards, adopted by revolutionary France.

name: Railway time
desc: A single standard time across Britain's railways, replacing local solar time.

name: Time zones
desc: Dividing the world into standard time regions offset from Greenwich.

name: Daylight saving time
desc: Shifting clocks forward in summer to extend evening daylight.

name: International System of Units
desc: The modern metric system of seven base units, used by science worldwide.

name: Geographic information system
desc: Computer systems for storing and analyzing mapped data, started in Canada.

name: Library
desc: Organized collections of written records, from Mesopotamian archives onward.

name: Platonic Academy
desc: Plato's school in Athens, a model for later institutions of learning.

name: Library of Alexandria
desc: The great Hellenistic library and research center of the ancient world.

name: Encyclopedia
desc: A comprehensive reference work, from Pliny's Natural History onward.

name: House of Wisdom
desc: Baghdad's center of translation and scholarship in the Islamic Golden Age.

name: University
desc: Self-governing communities of scholars granting degrees, starting at Bologna.

name: Royal Society
desc: London's society for experimental science, a model for scientific academies.

name: Scientific journal
desc: Periodicals that publish research results, starting with Philosophical Transactions.

name: Encyclopédie
desc: Diderot and d'Alembert's Enlightenment encyclopedia, which documented crafts and technology.

name: Dewey Decimal Classification
desc: A numeric scheme for shelving library books by subject.

name: Wikipedia
desc: A free online encyclopedia written collaboratively by volunteers.
